conversational_flow_notes: Five-line, two-speaker call-and-response with no overlapping speech or interruptions; every line waits for the prior line to fully end before starting. SPEAKER_01 opens and closes the exchange (lines 1, 3, 5), SPEAKER_00 supplies the two reactive/challenging lines (2, 4), giving the dialogue a symmetric A-B-A-B-A shape that sets up a question, gets deflected, then gets called out, then gets deflected again.
speech_rhythm_notes: Gaps between lines tighten and loosen with the joke structure: the 0.89s pause before line 2 ('What did you tell her?', 5 words) is the longest gap between any two spoken lines, giving SPEAKER_00's set-up question room to land as a beat of suspicion. Line 4 ('We figured it out three years ago.', 7 words), the exchange's zinger, follows the second-longest inter-line pause (0.64s) after line 3's deflection. The closing button line 5 ('She doesn't need to know that.', 6 words) has the shortest lead-in pause of the back half (0.42s), keeping the comeback snappy, but per silence_pauses.json it is followed by roughly 3.2s of near-continuous silence (four separate pause windows between 8.85s and 12.91s) after it ends -- by far the longest quiet stretch in the whole clip -- indicating the edit holds on a reaction shot to let the punchline breathe rather than cutting immediately.
